settings.text: Maison de Joaillerie
Flowers, kept
Jewellery drawn from botanical form and finished by hand, between Italy and India.

settings.title: Studied
settings.text: Every form begins with a real flower, observed before it is drawn.

settings.title: Made
settings.text: Built by hand in small numbers, in an atelier rather than a factory.

settings.title: Worn
settings.text: Weighted and finished to sit comfortably against the body, every day.

settings.statement: A flower lasts a season. Held in metal, it lasts a life.
settings.text:
Florève begins where botany and metalwork meet. Each form is studied from a living flower, then rebuilt by hand — petal by petal — in materials chosen to hold that shape long after the season has passed.

The result is not a copy of nature. It is nature, given a second structure.

settings.heading: The pieces we are known for

settings.text: Botany
Why a flower?
Because nothing else is asked to be beautiful and brief at the same time.

A flower is the shape a living thing makes when it has something to say. It opens once, completely, and then it is gone — which is precisely why it has been carried, pressed, painted and worn for as long as people have made things at all.

Our work begins there: not with an ornament that resembles a flower, but with the particular gesture of one. The turn of a petal at its edge. The way a stem carries weight it was never built for.

settings.heading: Where would you like to begin?

settings.text: Craft
Two hands, two countries
Drawn with Italian proportion. Finished with Indian patience.

A Florève piece passes through more hands than a machine-made one ever could. The line comes first — the restraint of a European drawing table, where a petal is reduced until only its gesture remains.

Then the work moves to the bench, where setting, finishing and polishing are done slowly, in the way that ornament has been made on the subcontinent for centuries. Neither tradition is decoration for the other. The piece needs both.

settings.title: The study
settings.text: A flower is photographed, measured and drawn before a single line is committed to metal.

settings.title: The bench
settings.text: Forms are shaped, soldered and set by hand, one piece at a time.

settings.title: The finish
settings.text: Surfaces are polished by hand until the light moves across them the way it moves across a petal.

settings.heading: From a living thing to a lasting one

settings.text: Made by hand
Drawn from botany
Finished in small numbers
Italy and India

settings.quote: Ornament is not decoration. It is the part of us we choose to make visible.

settings.heading: Find the one that is yours
settings.text: Every piece is made in small numbers. Take your time — and write to us if you would like to see one in person.
